scope: Claim-level cannabinoid polyketide, prenylation, oxidocyclase, synthase-locus, and alkyl side-chain evidence for THC-ENC-228 through THC-ENC-233.
rules: Purified-enzyme and heterologous-expression evidence establishes biochemical capability but does not by itself establish intact-plant rate limitation or crop concentration.
Synthase-locus structure and marker behavior are population- and assembly-dependent; sequence similarity alone must not be treated as universal chemotype prediction.
Minor-pathway and alkyl-homolog claims must distinguish dedicated enzyme evidence, substrate variation, promiscuity, inheritance, and analytical detection.
All mappings remain pending independent science review.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cannabis olivetolic acid formation requires tetraketide synthase together with olivetolic acid cyclase, and the pathway uses a hexanoyl-CoA-derived polyketide precursor.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Stout et al. 2012 precursor evidence; Gagne et al. 2012 abstract/results demonstrating OAC-dependent olivetolic acid formation.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the TKS/OAC route to olivetolic acid and separates established enzyme chemistry from whole-plant flux claims.
claimEvidence.limitations: Purified-enzyme and trichome-expression evidence does not establish the quantitative rate-limiting step in every intact cannabis genotype.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cannabis/hemp prenyltransferase activity can convert olivetolic acid plus GPP to CBGA, which serves as a major branch-point substrate for downstream cannabinoid acid synthases.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Fellermeier and Zenk 1998 enzyme study; Laverty et al. 2019 aromatic-prenyltransferase mapping/genetic context.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports CBGA as a central precursor while retaining later-enzyme and genotype context.
claimEvidence.limitations: The specific prenyltransferase contribution and branch-point pool behavior vary by genotype and pathway context; 'mother of all cannabinoids' is an oversimplification.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: THCA synthase directly catalyzes oxidative cyclization of CBGA to THCA, while the THCAS/CBDAS genomic region is structurally complex and should not be interpreted by short marker or similarity calls alone.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Sirikantaramas et al. 2004 cloning/heterologous expression/biochemistry; Laverty et al. 2019 synthase-locus structural mapping.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the biochemical THCA-forming step and cautious genotype-to-chemotype interpretation.
claimEvidence.limitations: Enzyme identity and locus genotype do not uniquely determine absolute THCA concentration because expression, precursor supply, development, environment, sampling, and analysis also contribute.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: CBDA synthase directly catalyzes oxidative cyclization of CBGA to CBDA, and CBDAS sits within a structurally complex cannabinoid synthase region whose genotype-to-phenotype interpretation requires context.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Taura et al. 2007 recombinant CBDAS study; Laverty et al. 2019 synthase-locus mapping.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the biochemical CBDA-forming step and separation of enzyme identity from whole-plant concentration.
claimEvidence.limitations: CBDAS genotype alone does not establish absolute CBDA/CBD concentration across genotypes and environments.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: A cannabis gene encoding CBCA synthase has been identified and its catalytic conversion of CBGA to CBCA characterized, demonstrating a dedicated biochemical basis for CBCA formation within a structurally complex oxidocyclase family.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Laverty et al. 2019 CBCAS identification, Pichia expression, HPLC product confirmation, purification, kinetics, and tissue-expression analysis.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports a dedicated CBCAS pathway while acknowledging related synthase-family complexity.
claimEvidence.limitations: Minor cannabinoid production can also reflect substrate availability, enzyme promiscuity, alternate pathways, and analytical context; a single gene call does not explain all minor cannabinoids.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cannabis propyl/pentyl cannabinoid side-chain composition shows complex inheritance with evidence for linkage, epistasis, dominance, and lineage-specific effects rather than one simple universal locus.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Welling et al. 2019 F2 segregation/genotype analysis and conclusion.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports alternate alkyl-side-chain pathways and cautious interpretation of varin cannabinoid genetics.
claimEvidence.limitations: The studied cross does not establish a universal inheritance model for all germplasm, and biochemical precursor supply must be distinguished from marker association.

note: Evidence IDs renumbered to preserve uniqueness after concurrent Batch 012 expansion. Batch 013 remains supplementary evidence for THC-ENC-228–233.
